question: Overcrowding, difficulties in accessing healthcare and psychological support and the resulting increase in cases of suicide and self-harm are undermining the dignity and rights of prison inmates and hindering their social reintegration.

Prison staff, for their part, often struggle with personnel shortages, long shifts, inmate assaults, occupational stress and the prospect of burnouts, and the available preventive and psychological support measures are inadequate.

Caring for inmates and supporting prison staff go hand-in-hand, as inadequate working conditions have a direct bearing on inmate safety, the quality of the care and support afforded to detainees and the effectiveness of inmate training and education pathways. In the light of Articles 1, 2, 4, 31 and 35 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights, Directive 89/391/EEC and Recommendation (EU) 2023/861: 1.

How will the Commission bolster European monitoring of detention and working conditions in prisons by pushing for the adoption of comparable data concerning overcrowding, suicides, healthcare provision, cases of assault, staffing levels statistics and the physical and mental well-being of prisoners and staff alike?

What initiatives will the Commission put forward to support Member States in improving detention and working conditions, particularly as regards suicide prevention, the safety of detainees and staff, training programmes and psychological support?
What European financial instruments will it use to support the social reintegration of prisoners and the improvement of the safety, training and working conditions of prison staff?
